doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

title: Lead sheets, lyrics and memorizing
summary: Nobody sends him lyrics or lead sheets so he makes his own, and he memorizes music such as a Bach cello suite.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Do you like to have a separate lyric sheet to read?
I never get that. But I sometimes will write out the lyric sheet.
No kidding? I don't know if something —

They don't even send me a lead sheet. Most of these kids can't do that you know. You know we create our own lead sheet. That's one of the first things I do is somehow I give myself a lead sheet and I write down the important words on the lead sheet so I know where I am at in the song and I know where — yeah — I do that myself.
Okay. It really makes you own the song I think, to go to that extra work and do it yourself. It sort of really gets it implanted in your head.

Yeah that's the whole point to do it is like but even when I was a little boy to learn a concerto or something until it was in my head I didn't know it. You've got to memorize, like right now I'm re—learning the fourth Bach Suite cello—wise. So I've been working on the prelude a lot this week and I almost have the whole thing memorized now for the second or third time in my lifetime.
